Type.description: Determines which action is performed when the button is clicked. Only populate the nested config object that matches the selected type; leave others null.

Events.description: Additional event handlers triggered after the button action completes. Uses the same event structure as the base component Events property.

Modal.description: Configuration for opening a component in a modal dialog. Active when Type = Modal. Specifies which component to display (Target) and how the dialog looks (Display).

Link.description: Configuration for navigating to a URL. Active when Type = Link. Supports internal Angular routes and external URLs.

Function.description: Configuration for calling a named JavaScript function. Active when Type = Function. The function must be registered in the application's formShared service.

ComponentAction.description: Configuration for triggering a named action on another component. Active when Type = ComponentAction. Targets any named component on the page by ComponentName and invokes actions like "data" (reload), "validate", "save", "schemaAndData".

EventBase.description:
Defines a single declarative event handler that one component dispatches to another when a named event fires
(e.g. onChange, onClick, onValueChange, onDataLoaded).
Use as an entry inside a component's events dictionary to wire cross-component communication
without writing JavaScript — populating fields from a fetched record, toggling section visibility,
locking inputs, raising toasts, chaining DataFetchers, or forwarding to another component's pass-through action.
When to use this vs. alternatives:
Reacting to another component's event (value change, data load, click) → Events / EventBase.
Computing a property from this component's own state (no fetch, reactive) →
      PropertyConverters.
Loading server data on a field change and mutating other fields →
      DataFetcher + its onValueChange events (still EventBase entries).
Custom AJAX or complex timing the declarative DSL can't express → ComponentScript escape hatch.
Two action families — see Action for the full verb list and semantics:
Pass-through verbs (data, validate, schema, schemaAndData,
      save, saveAndClose) forward to the target's ActionService.triggerComponentAction.
Mutation verbs (setValue, clearValue, setReadonly, setRequired,
      toggleVisible, notify, setProperty) imperatively update target state via the
      FormSharedService bridge, the same channel that backs the legacy frm.* JS API.
Expression DSL — ValueExpression and When run in a sandboxed JS evaluator
with { result, source, form } in scope plus ${...} token interpolation
(${componentName.@data.field}, ${@user.role}, ${@form.valid},
${@request.path.parameters.id}, bare ${FieldName} for parent-form FormControl values).
Standard JS operators, ternaries, optional chaining, array methods, and parseInt/.includes
are supported; window, document, fetch, eval, and storage APIs are blocked.
Constraints:
Emitter must be mounted inside a DGF FormComponent; cross-form dispatch is not supported.
Targets must be real DGF components (matched by ComponentName) — non-DGF DOM nodes
      cannot be targeted. Exception: notify is global and ignores ComponentName.
Multiple handlers in one event array execute in declared order; sequence mutations before
      pass-through reloads (setValue then data) to avoid clobbering.
Handlers are skipped silently when When is falsy.
See Events.md
for the full handler reference, action-verb matrix, and copy-paste recipes.
Auto-populate a name input and lock a section after a fetch:
{
  "events": {
    "onValueChange": [
      { "componentName": "fullNameInput",  "action": "setValue",      "valueExpression": "result.FirstName + ' ' + result.LastName" },
      { "componentName": "appealsSection", "action": "toggleVisible", "valueExpression": "result.IsEligible === true" },
      { "componentName": "structureCombo", "action": "setReadonly",   "valueExpression": "result.total === 1" }
    ]
  }
}

Name.description: The name of this event handler entry. Typically identifies the handler within the list for debugging purposes.

ComponentName.description: Name of the target component to trigger when this event fires. Must match the Name property of an existing component on the current page or form context.

Action.description:
Action to invoke on the target component when this event fires.
Existing actions: data (reload data), validate, schema,
schemaAndData, save, saveAndClose.
New mutation verbs (used with DataFetcher onValueChange events,
Button onClick events, and any component event that needs to imperatively update the UI):
VerbEffect on target
setValue
      Sets the target component's value to the result of ValueExpression
      evaluated against { result, source, form }. Works on any input component.
clearValue
      Forces the target component's value to null/empty. Equivalent to
      setValue with ValueExpression = "null" but more explicit and readable.
setReadonly
      Toggles the readonly flag on the target component.
      ValueExpression must evaluate to a boolean.
setRequired
      Toggles the required flag on the target component.
      ValueExpression must evaluate to a boolean.
toggleVisible
      Sets the hidden flag on the target component to
      !ValueExpression (i.e., the component is visible when
      ValueExpression is truthy). Works on any component including sections.
notify
      Shows a toast/inline notification. Uses Message and
      Severity. ComponentName is ignored for this verb —
      notification is global.
setProperty
      Sets an arbitrary named property on the target component. Use
      PropertyName to specify which property and ValueExpression
      for its value. Useful for updating labels, colors, CSS classes, and other display
      properties that are not covered by the other verbs.
Expression context for ValueExpression and When:
{ result, source, form } where result is the raw dataSource response,
source is the component that emitted the event, and form is the parent
form model (if applicable). The existing PropertyConverters expression evaluator
(execSecureEval in utils.ts) is reused — supported operators:
===, !==, ==, !=, &&, ||,
.includes(), parseInt(), array literals.
Token interpolation — the same ${...} syntax that PropertyConverters
support is also resolved before evaluation, so expressions can reference other
components and global accessors without going through result:
${componentName.@data.value}, ${@user.role}, ${@form.valid},
${@request.path.parameters.id}, ${@i18n('key', 'fallback')}.
Mix freely with the event-context variables — e.g.,
"when": "result.total > 0 && ${@user.role} === 'Admin'".
Auto-select and lock a child dropdown when parent yields exactly one match:
{ "componentName": "structureCombo", "action": "setValue",
  "valueExpression": "result.total === 1 ? result.items[0].key : null",
  "when": "result.total !== undefined" }
Show a warning notification when a duplicate record is detected:
{ "action": "notify", "when": "result.total > 0",
  "message": "This combination already exists.", "severity": "warning" }

Parameters.description: Additional parameters forwarded to the target component when the action is triggered. Supports the same token syntax as ComponentParameter: ${componentName}, ${item.fieldName}, ~UserID, ~NOW. Use to pass context from the event source (e.g., the submitted form's record ID) to the target component.

ValueExpression.description:
JavaScript expression evaluated in the Angular browser context against { result, source, form }.
The resolved value is applied as follows depending on Action:
setValue / setProperty — the expression result becomes the new property value.
setReadonly / setRequired — the expression result is coerced to boolean.
toggleVisible — component is shown when truthy, hidden when falsy.
clearValue / notify — this field is ignored.
Supports token syntax: result.FieldName, result.total === 1,
result.items[0].key, parseInt(result.count) > 0.
Optional — when omitted for setValue, the raw result object is used as-is.

When.description:
Optional JavaScript gate expression evaluated against { result, source, form } before
the action is dispatched. When set, the action is skipped if this expression evaluates
to falsy. Supports the same syntax as ValueExpression.
Example — only clear when the check returns results:
"when": "result.total > 0"

Message.description:
Notification text displayed to the user when Action is notify.
Supports inline HTML for formatted messages. Ignored for all other action verbs.

Severity.description:
Severity level for notify action. Controls toast styling.
Accepted values: info (default), success, warning, error.
Ignored for all other action verbs.

PropertyName.description:
Name of the property to set on the target component when Action is
setProperty. Must be a valid camelCase property name of the target component's model
(e.g., "label", "cssClass", "color"). The value is supplied via
ValueExpression. Ignored for all other action verbs.

ModalActionConfig.description: Full config for a modal action: what to open + how the dialog looks.

Target.description: Specifies which component to open in the modal dialog — its type (Form, Workflow, ProcessFlow, Router) and its Name.

Display.description: Controls the visual appearance of the modal dialog — title, dimensions, and interactive options.

ModalTargetConfig.description: What component to open in the modal.

TargetType.description: The type of component to render inside the modal. Use Form for data entry, Workflow for multi-step processes, ProcessFlow for approval flows, Router for embedded navigation.

TargetName.description: The Name of the component configuration to load and render inside the modal dialog.

ButtonTargetType.description:
Identifies which component type a button action will open.
Designed to be extended with new component types in future iterations.
Only includes component types that can be meaningfully opened from a button click.

ModalDisplayConfig.description: How the modal dialog window looks. Replaces ButtonActionModal.

Title.description: Text displayed in the modal dialog header bar.

Width.description: Modal dialog width as a CSS value (e.g., "50vw", "800px"). Defaults to "80vw" when omitted.

Closable.description: When true (default), displays an X button allowing users to close the modal without completing the action.

Maximizable.description: When true (default), displays a maximize button allowing users to expand the modal to full screen.

Height.description: Modal dialog height as a CSS value (e.g., "400px", "80vh"). Defaults to "auto" when omitted.

ShowCloseButton.description: When true, displays a Close button in the modal footer at the bottom. Default: false. Leave unset when hosting a Form with its own Cancel action to avoid duplicate controls. Useful for read-only views, Workflow, ProcessFlow or Router targets that don't expose their own close button.

CloseButtonLabel.description: Label for the bottom close button. Accepts a translation key. Defaults to "button_label_close" when omitted.

LinkActionConfig.description: Config for a link navigation action.

Href.description: Target URL for navigation. Use Angular route paths (e.g., "/services/123") for internal navigation or absolute URLs for external links.

Target.description: Browser window target for the navigation. "_blank" opens in a new tab, "_self" (default) navigates in the current tab.

FunctionActionConfig.description: Config for invoking a named client-side JS function.

Name.description: Name of the JavaScript function to call. The function must be registered in the application's formShared service at startup.

ComponentActionConfig.description: Config for triggering an ActionName on a named component.

TargetName.description: Name property of the target component to trigger the action on. Must match a component's Name on the current page.

TargetAction.description: Action to invoke on the target component. Common values: "data" (reload component data), "validate" (trigger validation), "schema" (reload schema), "schemaAndData" (reload both), "save" (submit form data), "saveAndClose" (save and close modal).

Label.description: Display label shown above the input field in the UI.

Required.description: When true, the field must have a non-empty value before the parent form can be submitted. Triggers built-in validation and displays an error message if left empty.

Readonly.description: When true, the field value is displayed but cannot be edited by the user. Differs from Disabled in that readonly fields still participate in form submission and validation.

Disabled.description: When true, the field is rendered in a disabled state and excluded from form submission. Use to prevent interaction with fields that are not applicable given the current context.

StorageKey.description: Key used to persist component state (data, value, selection) in browser session/local storage. When set, the component restores its last state on page reload.

Hidden.description: When true, the component is not rendered in the UI. Use propertyConverters.hidden to make this conditional at runtime based on data values.

Type.description: Discriminator that determines which Angular component is rendered. Must match a ComponentType enum value verbatim — values are PascalCase: "Form", "DataTable", "ComboBox", "Text", "Button", "Calendar", etc. (lowercase or camelCase will fail validation). The UI factory uses this to instantiate the correct Angular component class.

Uid.description: Optional secondary unique identifier. Used internally for tracking and correlation when Name alone is insufficient.

Name.description: Unique identifier for this component instance within the application. Used to reference this component from events (as ComponentName target), parameters (as ${Name} token), button ComponentAction targets, and the ref binding system. Must be unique per page/form context.

Path.description: File system path used to load this component's configuration from an external JSON file. When set, the SiteMapManager replaces this component with the fully resolved content loaded from the specified path. Enables reusable component definitions stored as separate files.

Description.description: Human-readable description of this component's purpose. Used for accessibility annotations and documentation; not displayed in the UI by default.

Cols.description: Width of this component in Bootstrap grid columns (1–12). Components are arranged in 12-column rows; use Cols=6 for half-width, Cols=12 for full-width. Omit to use the component's default width.

Ref.description:
Binds this component to a named data source declared on a parent Page or container, using dot-notation: "pageName.dataSourceName".
The UI resolves the bound data source from the component store and uses it as this component's display data.
IMPORTANT: If the component also has its own DataSource property configured, the component's own DataSource takes precedence over Ref.
Use Ref when this component shares an already-loaded page-level data source and does not need its own independent fetch.
Use an explicit DataSource instead when the component needs its own parameters, pagination, or filtering logic.
Example: a ListBox with Ref="servicePassportPage.whoCanApply" displays data from that page-level data source.

Compact.description: When true, applies compact/dense styling to reduce vertical spacing. Useful inside data-dense layouts such as DataTable row templates or sidebar panels.

MetaData.description: Arbitrary key-value metadata attached to this component. Special keys recognized by the framework: "requireUser" ("authenticated" or "guest") controls visibility based on auth state; "requireClaims" (array of claim filter objects) applies claim-based access control. The SiteMapManager strips nodes that fail these checks before serving to the client.

PropertyConverters.description:
Conditional property override map evaluated as JavaScript expressions at runtime in the Angular UI.
Structure: outer key = camelCase property name to override on THIS component (e.g., "required", "disabled",
"hidden", "readonly", "value", "color", "background"); inner key = JavaScript expression string
evaluated against the current data context using ${field} tokens; inner value = the property value
applied when the expression is truthy. All entries are evaluated; last matching expression wins.
Supported in expressions: ===, !==, ==, !=, &&, ||, .includes(), parseInt(), array literals.
Example — conditional icon/color based on status:
{ "value": { "${item.VerifyStatus.key} === '2'": "dge-status-failed" },
  "color": { "${item.VerifyStatus.key} === '2'": "red", "${item.VerifyStatus.key} != '2'": "green" } }
Example — make field readonly when count is zero:
{ "readonly": { "parseInt(${AttachCount}) == 0": true, "parseInt(${AttachCount}) != 0": false } }
Example — complex visibility with array check:
{ "hidden": { "['10','31'].includes(${passport.ServiceID}) && ${User.currentEntityId} === ''": true } }
Use AddPropertyConverter(propertyName, valueToAssign, expressionToCheck) as a C# server-side helper.

Parameters.description:
Parameters sent with every data request from this component. They serve four distinct roles:
            
ROLE 1 — SERVER CONTEXT: Forward fixed or user-session values to the data source.
  Example: [{ "name": "CreatedBy", "value": "~UserID" }, { "name": "AppId", "value": "~APPLICATIONID" }]
            
ROLE 2 — FILTER / SEARCH: Narrow DataSource results server-side.
  Example: [{ "name": "StatusId", "value": "1" }]  — only active records
            
ROLE 3 — REQUEST GATING: When required=true, the request is blocked until the value is non-empty.
  Use this to prevent a component from fetching until a dependency is satisfied.
  Example: [{ "name": "CaseId", "value": "${caseCombo}", "required": true }]
  The component will not fire any request until caseCombo has a value.
            
ROLE 4 — REACTIVE CASCADING: Bind to another component's value using ${componentName}.
  The Angular UI watches the resolved value; when it changes, the component automatically
  re-fetches its data with the new parameter value. This is the standard pattern for
  dependent dropdowns (e.g., Country → District).
  Example: District ComboBox: [{ "name": "CountryId", "value": "${countryCombo}", "required": true }]
  When the user selects a country, District re-fetches filtered to that country.
  required=true also prevents District from fetching before Country is selected.
            
MIRRORING RULE: Every parameter declared in the DataSource's Parameters list must also appear
here so the Angular UI knows to collect and forward it. Exception: "page" and "pageSize" are
auto-forwarded from Paging — do NOT add them manually.
            
For the full list of value expression syntax (component accessors, global accessors, system tokens),
see ComponentParameter.Value documentation.

ComponentScript.description: Script hooks executed in the Angular browser context for this component. Use to implement client-side logic that reacts to component lifecycle events without server round-trips.

Events.description:
Cross-component event handlers. Key = event name emitted by this component type:
Forms emit "onSubmited", "onDeleted", "onLoaded"; Uploaders emit "onUploaded", "onDeleted";
Inputs/ComboBoxes emit "onChange", "onClick"; DataTable emits "onRowSelected", "onRowDeleted".
Each list entry targets another component by ComponentName and triggers an Action on it.
Available actions: "data" (reload data), "validate", "schema", "schemaAndData", "save", "saveAndClose".
Entries can include their own Parameters list with token syntax to forward event payload context.
Example — after Form submits, trigger EligibilityComponent to re-validate:
{ "onSubmited": [{ "componentName": "eligibility-component", "action": "validate",
  "parameters": [{ "name": "CaseId", "value": "${item.data.CaseId}", "required": true }] }] }

Validators.description:
Declarative custom validators attached to this component. Each entry contributes to the parent
FormGroup.valid channel — failing validators block NEXT/SAVE through the existing gate.
For aggregating components without a real FormControl (DataTable, DocumentGrid, ...), the
framework registers a shadow FormControl named <Name>__validity on the parent
FormGroup that carries the validator's errors.
Component names containing the reserved infix __ are rejected at form load.
See ValidatorBase for the entry shape and the validator reference docs at
get_doc_page('Components/Behavior/Validators.md').

Messages.description: Validation and informational messages attached to this component. Populated by the server-side Validate() method when configuration is invalid. Also used by the UI to display inline error/warning/info messages below the component.

CssClass.description: One or more CSS class names (space-separated) applied to the component's root element. Supports both Bootstrap utility classes and application-specific design system classes.

Name.description: Parameter key name sent to the data source. Must match the parameter name declared in the DataSource's Parameters list and the server-side handler.

Value.description:
Value or binding expression for this parameter. Can be a literal string or any of the following token types:
            
COMPONENT TOKENS (reactive — re-fetches when source changes):
  ${componentName}                        — primary bound value of a named component (input, combo, etc.)
  ${componentName.@properties.propName}   — a schema property of another component
  ${componentName.@parameters.paramName}  — a parameter value of another component
  ${componentName.@data.field.subField}   — nested data field loaded by another component
            
ROW CONTEXT TOKENS (only valid inside DataTable column templates / row actions):
  ${item.ColumnName}                      — field from the current DataTable row
  ${item.Nested.Field}                    — nested field from the current row
            
GLOBAL / USER TOKENS:
  ${@user.currentEntityId}                — authenticated user's entity ID
  ${@user.currentRoleName}                — authenticated user's role
  ${@user.fullName}                       — user display name
  ${@request.path.parameters.id}          — current route path parameter
  ${@request.query.parameters.search}     — current URL query parameter
  ${@settings.apiUrl}                     — application setting value
  ${@i18n('key', 'default')}              — translated string
  ${formName.@form.valid}                 — Angular form validity boolean
            
SYSTEM TOKENS (resolved server-side):
  ~UserID          — current authenticated user ID
  ~NOW             — current server timestamp
  ~APPLICATIONID   — current application ID
            
Literal values (no token) are sent as-is: "value": "1", "value": "Active"

Required.description:
When true, the component's data request is blocked (not sent) until this parameter resolves to a non-null, non-empty value.
This is the primary mechanism for two patterns:
            
REQUEST GATING: Prevent a fetch from firing with incomplete data.
  Example: a DataTable that must not load until a case is selected in a ComboBox.
  [{ "name": "CaseId", "value": "${caseCombo}", "required": true }]
            
CASCADE GUARD: Combined with a ${componentName} binding, required=true ensures a dependent
  component (e.g., District dropdown) does not fetch until its parent (e.g., Country) has a value.
  When the parent value clears, the child's request is blocked again automatically.
            
When false or omitted, missing/empty parameter values are forwarded as-is and the request fires regardless.

RequiredMessage.description: Custom message displayed when this required parameter cannot be resolved. Defaults to a generic "missing required parameter" message if omitted.

OnValueChange.description: JavaScript code string executed in the browser each time this component's value changes. Use to calculate derived field values, conditionally show/hide other components, or enforce cross-field business rules without server round-trips. Has access to the component's Angular context and the NGXS store via injected services.

ValidatorBase.description:
Defines a declarative custom validator attached to a DGF component. Used to express
business validity rules that participate in the same FormGroup.valid channel
that already gates NEXT and SAVE — including rules on aggregating components
(DataTable, DocumentGrid, RichSection) that have no real FormControl.
            
When to use this vs. alternatives:
"All rows of a DataTable must satisfy a row predicate" → ValidatorBase.
"Sum of allocations must equal 100%" → ValidatorBase on the parent or aggregating component.
"Field must match a regex" → built-in Pattern / Angular validator, NOT this.
"Toggle a field's visibility based on another field" → PropertyConverters.
            
Expression DSL — Expression, When, Message, and
Severity run in a sandboxed JS evaluator with { value, source, form } in scope
(Phase 2 adds result / fetcher-key context for backend validators) plus ${...} token
interpolation. Standard JS operators, ternaries, optional chaining, array methods, and
parseInt/.includes are supported. window, document, fetch,
eval, and storage APIs are blocked.
            
Form gating contract:
For a component with a real FormControl, a failing validator sets control.errors[key],
      which makes FormGroup.valid false and gates NEXT/SAVE.
For an aggregating component (DataTable, …) without a FormControl, the framework registers a
      shadow FormControl named <componentName>__validity on the parent FormGroup that
      carries the validator's errors. The shadow is hidden from ${...} token resolution.
Validators with Severity = Warning or Info never mark the form invalid; they
      render as advisories in the UI only.
            
See get_doc_page('Components/Behavior/Validators.md')
for the full reference and copy-paste recipes.
            
Block NEXT until every DataTable row is signed:
{
  "type": "dataTable",
  "name": "applicationsTable",
  "validators": [
    {
      "key": "allFormsSigned",
      "expression": "value.items.every(r => r.IsSigned === true)",
      "message": "All application forms must be signed before continuing."
    }
  ]
}

Key.description:
Stable identifier for this validator. Surfaces in FormControl.errors[key] and is the address
authors use when programmatically clearing the error (e.g. frm.clearCustomErrors(name)).
Required. Must be unique within a single component's validators[] array.

Expression.description:
JavaScript expression. Returns true / truthy when the rule is satisfied (valid),
or false / falsy / a string when the rule fails (invalid). When the expression
returns a string, that string is used as the error message — overriding Message.
Required. Evaluated in the sandboxed evaluator with { value, source, form } in scope.

Message.description:
Error text rendered when Expression evaluates to falsy.
Supports ${...} token interpolation against the same evaluation context as Expression
— e.g. "Only ${value.signedCount} of ${value.totalCount} items are signed.".
Missing tokens render as empty strings; the validator still applies.

When.description:
Optional gate. When set and evaluates to falsy, the validator is SKIPPED (treated as valid) for the
current render. Use to conditionally apply rules — e.g. "passport docs required only when applicant is foreign".
Same expression DSL as Expression.

ValidateOn.description:
Determines when the validator runs. Defaults to onChange.
onChange — re-evaluates reactively whenever the component value or any referenced token changes.
      The engine caches fetcher results by parameter snapshot, so expensive backend probes only re-fire when their inputs change.
onSave — deferred to save time. Use for backend probes that are too expensive to fire reactively
      (duplicate lookups, rate-limited external services). The submit flow awaits any pending probe through
      the save-time barrier before reading form.valid.
For explicit-only firing (polling, "Re-check" buttons), compose onChange with a sibling DataFetcher's
manualTrigger flag and the revalidate event verb. A separate manual trigger value was
considered and rejected as gratuitous complexity.

Severity.description:
Severity of the failure. Accepts the literal values "error", "warning", or "info",
OR a ${...} token expression that resolves to one of those at evaluation time
(e.g. "${result.data.severity}" in a backend-driven validator). Invalid resolution
falls back to "error" with a one-time warning in the browser console.
Defaults to "error". Only "error" contributes to FormGroup.invalid;
"warning" and "info" are advisory-only.

DataFetcher.description:
Inline single-fetcher sugar (Phase 2). The probe result is exposed to Expression
and Message as the local variable result — equivalent to
DataFetchers = { ["result"] = value }. Mutually exclusive with DataFetchers
and Fetcher. When more than one is set the mapper applies priority order:
Fetcher → DataFetcher → DataFetchers.

DataFetchers.description:
Inline multi-fetcher map (Phase 2). Each entry's resolved envelope is exposed to
Expression and Message by its key — e.g. a map entry
"dup" surfaces as dup.ok, dup.data, dup.error.
Reserved keys: value, source, form, result
(the last reserved only when this property is used — collides with the
DataFetcher sugar). Mutually exclusive with DataFetcher
and Fetcher. When more than one is set the mapper applies priority order:
Fetcher → DataFetcher → DataFetchers.

Fetcher.description:
Named reference to a sibling <dataFetcher> component on the same form (Phase 2 escape hatch).
Use when the validator needs the full DataFetcher surface (events, manualTrigger,
NGXS-addressable result) instead of the narrow inline definition. Mutually exclusive with
DataFetcher and DataFetchers.

InlineDataFetcherDefinition.description:
Inline, validator-private data-fetcher definition. Narrow projection of DataFetcher
(the full headless DataFetcher component) carrying only the fields a validator needs to issue
an HTTP probe against a backend dataSource and expose the response to its expression.
            
Used by DataFetcher (singular sugar) and
DataFetchers (plural map). Differs from a fully-fledged
DataFetcher component in three deliberate ways:
No name — fetcher results are addressed by validator-map key, never by
      a global registry name. Validator-scoped only.
No manualTrigger — validators fire reactively when their context changes;
      there is no Button → ComponentAction handoff for inline probes.
No events — fetcher output flows into the validator's expression context
      ({ dup, bl, fund, ... }), not into the form-wide event dispatcher.
            
Authors needing the full DataFetcher surface (events, manualTrigger, NGXS-addressable
result) should declare a sibling <dataFetcher> component on the form and reference it
from the validator via Fetcher.
            
Duplicate-applicant check on an NRC field:
{
  "dataSourcePath": "validators/CheckDuplicateApplicant",
  "parameters": [
    { "name": "NRC", "value": "${value}", "required": true }
  ]
}

DataSourcePath.description:
Relative path to the backend dataSource the validator probes. Server-only —
stripped from the client payload at UI-mapping time and replaced by Uid
(see IValidatorFetcherSanitizer), so the backend dataSource path never reaches the
browser. Resolved by the runtime fetcher service the same way as the full DataFetcher
component. Required on the authored/server-side definition.

Uid.description:
Opaque, per-session handle the client uses to invoke this probe without ever seeing the
backend dataSource path. Populated at UI-mapping time by IValidatorFetcherSanitizer,
which caches the path server-side and nulls DataSourcePath on the client copy.
Null on the server-side configuration. When set, the probe is resolved server-side from the
cached configuration keyed by this uid (the same uid → config → dataSourcePath path the
DataFetcher component uses).

Parameters.description:
Parameter bindings sent with the probe. Supports the same token DSL as
Value plus the validator-local sandbox identifier
${value} (the host component's current value).

ValueExpression.description:
Optional post-processing expression evaluated against the raw backend response.
When present, the validator's expression sees the expression result as data
instead of the raw payload. Same DSL as Expression.

Message.description: The message text displayed to the user in the component's message area.

Type.description: Severity level of this message. Info = informational note, Warning = non-blocking issue, Error = blocking validation failure, Success = positive feedback.

Position.description: Controls where the message is rendered relative to the component. Defaults to Bottom.

Hidden.description: When true, this message is not rendered in the UI regardless of its Type. Use to suppress messages programmatically without removing them from the collection.

PropertyConverters.description:
Conditional property override map evaluated as JavaScript expressions at runtime in the Angular UI.
Structure: outer key = camelCase property name to override on THIS component (e.g., "required", "disabled",
"hidden", "readonly", "value", "color", "background"); inner key = JavaScript expression string
evaluated against the current data context using ${field} tokens; inner value = the property value
applied when the expression is truthy. All entries are evaluated; last matching expression wins.
Supported in expressions: ===, !==, ==, !=, &&, ||, .includes(), parseInt(), array literals.
Example — conditional icon/color based on status:
{ "value": { "${item.VerifyStatus.key} === '2'": "dge-status-failed" },
  "color": { "${item.VerifyStatus.key} === '2'": "red", "${item.VerifyStatus.key} != '2'": "green" } }
Example — make field readonly when count is zero:
{ "readonly": { "parseInt(${AttachCount}) == 0": true, "parseInt(${AttachCount}) != 0": false } }
Example — complex visibility with array check:
{ "hidden": { "['10','31'].includes(${passport.ServiceID}) && ${User.currentEntityId} === ''": true } }
Use AddPropertyConverter(propertyName, valueToAssign, expressionToCheck) as a C# server-side helper.

allOf.description:
Fundamental UI element for triggering user actions with multiple styling variants and interactive states.
            
PURPOSE: Trigger actions, open modals, navigate URLs, or initiate workflows.
            
FEATURES:
- Multiple styling variants (Button, Link, etc.) and accent styles (Primary, Secondary, Success, Danger, etc.)
- Icon positioning (left/right) with custom icon classes
- Tooltip and custom color support
- Toggle/stateful button behavior
- Cross-component event triggering through handlers
            
Based on PrimeNG Button component.

Text.description: Label text displayed on the button face.

Color.description: Text/icon color override for the button content.

Icon.description: Icon class name displayed on the button (e.g., "dge-add-file", "dge-eye"). Uses the application icon font.

IconPosition.description: Position of the icon relative to the button text. Left places icon before text, Right places icon after text.

Size.description: Button size variant. Controls padding and font size.

Style.description: Button shape/type variant (e.g., standard Button or other structural variants).

ButtonStyle.description: Visual accent style of the button (Primary, Secondary, Success, Danger, etc.). Controls background and border color.

Toggle.description: When true, the button maintains a pressed/unpressed visual state between clicks, behaving as a toggle switch.

Handler.description: Server-side handler identifier used to route button actions through a specific processing pipeline.

Action.description: Defines what happens when the button is clicked — opens a modal, navigates to a URL, calls a JS function, or triggers an action on another component.
